MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L13·N12049unmasked layer
This neuron fires at clause/sentence-boundary tokens (commas, periods, and the first word after them) in formal, impersonal expository prose — and is strongly *suppressed* at exactly the same boundary positions inside casual conversational replies ("Thanks, …", "Sorry, I live in CA.", "great prize! it's fun"), so it effectively marks punctuation-boundary register as expository rather than chatty.

L30·N149unmasked layer
This neuron weakly fires on short, common monosyllabic lowercase content words (mostly verbs like "read", "tell", "ask", "host", "heap") mid-sentence in ordinary flowing prose, while its strongest (negative) response is to single capital letters embedded in ALL-CAPS strings/acronyms (e.g. the "F" in PUFAs, "O" in LINALOOL/LOOOONG, "K" in 25KHz) — i.e. it is a prose-word vs. caps-token discriminator.
